data.content:
## Build Failure Analysis

**Solution:** `BuildDiag.sln` (3 projects: `Core`, `Services`, `Api`)

### Root Cause (1 error, 1 project)

**`Services.csproj`** — Missing NuGet package reference to `Newtonsoft.Json`

`Services/UserService.cs` uses `Newtonsoft.Json` and `Newtonsoft.Json.Linq` (lines 2–3) and the `JObject` type (line 22), but `Services.csproj` has **no `<PackageReference>` for `Newtonsoft.Json`**.

This produces 3 compiler errors (all CS0246):
| Line | Error |
|------|-------|
| 2:7 | Namespace `Newtonsoft` not found |
| 3:7 | Namespace `Newtonsoft` not found |
| 22:19 | Type `JObject` not found |

### Cascading Failure

- **`BuildDiag.sln`** — marked as failed because `Services.csproj` (a member project) failed.
- **`Api.csproj`** — references `Services.csproj` but appears to have built successfully in this run (no errors). In a stricter `/maxcpucount:1` build it could cascade.
- **`Core.csproj`** — built successfully (no errors).

### Fix

Add the missing package reference to `Services/Services.csproj`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Or, if the project intends to use the built-in `System.Text.Json` instead, replace the `using Newtonsoft.Json` / `JObject` usage with `System.Text.Json` equivalents.
